tax_burden.notes: Trading profits are taxed at 12.5%, one of the lowest headline company rates among peers, but the owner then pays a high personal charge on dividends: about 52% at the top once income tax, the universal social charge, and social insurance stack. Share-sale gains are taxed at 33%, with a 10% entrepreneur rate up to a lifetime cap. Employer social insurance is light at about 11% of pay. VAT 23% is customer-borne and excluded.

_meta.source: PwC Worldwide Tax Summaries Ireland and Revenue.ie (CIT 12.5% trading, CGT 33%, employer PRSI 11.25%, VAT 23%); KPMG/Revenue on the top combined dividend rate ~52.1% (40% income tax + 8% USC + ~4.1% PRSI). business_rates_pct_equiv modeled.
_meta.method: total_pct = corp + (1 - corp/100)*dividend + business_rates_equiv = 12.5 + 0.875*52.1 + 3 = 61.09. corporation_tax_pct is the 12.5% trading rate (non-trading income is 25%; trading rate used for an operating SME). dividend_tax_pct is the top marginal personal rate on dividends (income tax 40% + USC 8% + PRSI ~4.1%); a 3% surcharge can push it to ~55% at very high non-PAYE income. business_rates_pct_equiv modeled at 3% of profit for recurring commercial rates (local authority premises charge). capital_gains_pct 33% stored as component, excluded from total_pct.

_meta.source: Scores modeled from provided macro snapshot (GDP/cap PPP 133437, growth 2.5%, services 60.6%, mfg 29.6%, labour force 2.89M, business density 6.4) plus governance signal: Transparency International CPI 2024 score 76 (clean, top tier); common-law system and global multinational and capital hub; GDP/cap PPP inflated by multinational activity; high operating costs.
_meta.method: ease_of_business 8: common-law, business-friendly registration and contract enforcement. talent_pool 7: small 2.9M labour force, highly educated, tight for scaling. access_to_financing 8: strong banking plus global capital and VC presence. political_stability 9: high governance and stable pro-business policy (CPI 76). economic_reward 9: very high GDP/cap PPP (multinational-inflated) with steady growth. affordability 3: high labour, office and living costs.

banking.notes: A foreigner can open a business account, but the main banks prefer at least one resident or EU-based director and often need an in-person visit, so non-residents commonly use a fintech first. Goods sellers register for VAT at a higher turnover than services.

_meta.source: Registrar of companies fee schedule (EUR 50 online Form A1) and 5 to 10 working day processing; tax authority VAT thresholds page (EUR 42,500 services, EUR 85,000 goods, from 1 Jan 2025); company-formation and banking guides for the bond and bank process. VAT threshold shown is the services figure; goods threshold is EUR 85,000.
_meta.method: Held via official registrar fee page plus tax-authority VAT-thresholds page, corroborated by 3+ formation guides; converted EUR at fx_to_usd 1.146815; non-EEA bond cost modeled within the cited EUR 1,600 to 2,000 range.

notes.hire: Hiring is flexible by EU standards. Employer payroll on-costs are low, around 11% of pay, well below most of the euro area.
notes.contract: Written terms must be issued early. Fixed term contracts are allowed, but repeated renewals beyond four years convert to permanent.
notes.fire: After 12 months service, dismissal must be fair and follow procedure, with redress for unfair dismissal; probation gives early flexibility.
notes.recruiting: Deep English speaking talent base anchored by large tech and pharma multinationals, drawing heavily on EU and international hires.

_meta.source: Pay modeled from average gross earnings (~EUR 52.6k/year, weekly ~EUR 1,012) scaled to white-collar levels plus ~14% employer PRSI load (employer PRSI ~11.15-11.25%); FX 1.146815. Dismissal rules from unfair dismissal law (protection after 12 months). Languages from Census 2022 (English near-universal; ~39.8% claim some Irish ability, very few daily speakers).
_meta.method: White-collar base by level x low employer on-cost multiplier, converted to USD; talent_depth scored high for tech and pharma multinational clusters; English flagged native, Irish flagged not native given negligible first-language use.

_meta.source: EU income and living conditions survey 2024: mean equivalised net income EUR 37,267, median EUR 33,013; disposable income Gini 26.4 (agrees with OECD income distribution database 28.5, 2022). National accounts household consumption by purpose 2023: housing and utilities 26.3 pct, transport 9.6 pct, food and non-alcoholic 8.6 pct, recreation and culture 7.3 pct, restaurants and hotels 16.1 pct, furnishings and household equipment 4.3 pct. Local EUR converted at fx 1.146815.
_meta.method: Mean and median held on an equivalised net disposable per-person basis from two agreeing official sources. Top decile modeled at 2.4x median and top 1 percent at 5.6x median from the survey decile structure. Spend shares mapped from the consumption-by-purpose classification: housing_utilities=housing/water/energy, transport=transport, food_drink=food and non-alcoholic beverages, recreation=recreation and culture, dining_out=restaurants and hotels, household_goods=furnishings and household equipment, other holds the residual to sum 100.

_raw.income_basis: Annual equivalised household net disposable income on a per-person basis (after taxes and transfers). Mean and median held from official statistics. Top decile and top 1 percent modeled from the published income distribution.

_meta.source: Energy: Eurostat non-household medium-size electricity H2 2024 0.25 EUR/kWh (highest in EU); representative all-in 0.30 USD. Rent: Dublin prime office ~673 EUR/sqm/yr (65 USD/sqft, CBRE/Savills 2024); representative city-centre secondary 480 EUR/sqm/yr. Labour: full-time average earnings ~61,100 EUR/yr 2024 (CSO/Eurostat) x ~1.11 employer PRSI (~11.05-11.15%). Setup: CRO online incorporation 50 EUR mandatory, with formation agent + registered office typically 500-1,000 EUR; representative 600 EUR.
_meta.method: Local currency EUR. usd = local x 1.146815. Energy stated directly in USD. Rent 480 EUR/sqm/yr -> USD (representative below prime). Labour 61,100 x 1.11 = ~67,900 EUR -> USD. Setup 600 EUR -> USD.

_meta.source: Energy held: highest EU non-household electricity price H2-2025 (~0.255 EUR/kWh) per Eurostat. Skills held: record talent shortages, 83% of employers find the market challenging, 78% report IT shortages, housing named the #1 FDI risk per ManpowerGroup, AmCham, OECD Ireland 2025. Rule/tax moderate: 12.5% base retained with 2.5% Pillar Two top-up (QDTT) for large groups, small business largely unaffected, per PwC, Revenue, EY. Currency low: euro. Demand: 2.5% growth but MNC/trade-war exposed. Exit multiples modeled from UK&I mid-market EBITDA 5.3x (Dealsuite Sep-2025) with very wide small-firm gap (200k-EBITDA ~3.3x), mapped to owner-earnings SDE; active broker market and deal volume support active climate.
_meta.method: Energy and skills triangulated from 2+ sources; euro drives low currency score; Pillar Two scored low for small business; SDE multiples estimated from published UK&I small-firm EBITDA brackets discounted to owner-operator scale.

_meta.source: Anchor Dublin = primary business and political city. Dublin Region GDP roughly EUR248bn in 2023, over 40 percent of Irish GDP (Economy of Dublin / CSO County Incomes and Regional GDP). Cork is the clear second city and pharma/tech hub; Galway (medtech), Limerick (tech/pharma) and Waterford follow. Ireland headline GDP is distorted by multinational accounting, so secondary-city indices are kept conservative and based on city scale and FDI footprint rather than raw regional GDP.
_meta.method: Dublin = 100 anchor (dominant, >40 percent of national GDP). market_index_vs_capital modeled from relative city size, office market and FDI/employment footprint; secondary cities scaled well below Dublin given its extreme concentration.

_meta.source: Positions modeled from World Bank Worldwide Governance Indicators rule-of-law estimate (~1.59), WJP Rule of Law Index 2024 (top-15), Corruption Perceptions Index 2024 (~76-77), and Hofstede dimensions (PDI 28, IDV 70, UAI 35) plus Erin Meyer Culture Map (Anglo diplomatic-direct, egalitarian).
_meta.method: Spectrum positions 0-1 anchored to cross-country ordering of governance indicators (gov_business) and cross-cultural research (culture_outsider); 1 = right-hand label.
